title: Hanging File Story Decision Point Card Pack
audience: Families, homeschool groups, tutors, and adult-led writing tables for writers ages 7-11.
sessionLength: 16 printable hanging file story decision-point cards plus adult guide tools, decision-point routines, take-home decision slips, and optional adult prompts
safetyNote: No scary harm, no bullying, no romance, no weapons, no branded characters, and no identifying facts.

cover.kicker: Printable hanging file decision point cards
cover.headline: Hanging File Story Decision Point Card Pack
cover.subhead: Sixteen hanging-file cards help writers compare two pretend paths, choose one path, write a consequence note, and add a broad file label.
included: 16 printable hanging file decision point cards

adultGuide.title: Hanging File Decision Point Adult Guide
bullets: Set out one hanging file, blank pages, pencils, and a decision-point card before the adult-led paper start: ____________________.
Choose one fictional character choice and keep every path, clue, and consequence note invented: ____________________.
Move through character choice, path one, path two, clue to compare, chosen path, consequence note, and hanging-file label in order: ____________________.
Keep the adult in charge of the hanging file while the writer writes or dictates short paper lines: ____________________.
Use pretend characters, broad places, and invented actions only; skip real names, real places, and personal facts: ____________________.
Close by reading the chosen path, adding one consequence note, and writing the hanging-file label for later adult-led paper planning: ____________________.

decisionPointRoutines.title: Character Choice Start
decisionPointRoutines.materials: Hanging file, blank page, pencil, and character choice slip.
steps: The adult opens the hanging file and points to the character choice blank: ____________________.
The writer names one fictional character for the paper plan: ____________________.
The adult asks what choice is standing in front of that character: ____________________.
The writer writes or dictates one character choice line on paper: ____________________.
decisionPointRoutines.adultWrapLine: The decision point starts with this fictional character choice: ____________________.

decisionPointRoutines.title: Path One Fold
decisionPointRoutines.materials: Hanging file, current page, pencil, and path one slip.
steps: The adult rereads the character choice line from the page: ____________________.
The writer invents one path the fictional character could take: ____________________.
The adult asks what makes path one clear on paper: ____________________.
The writer writes path one on the slip and places it in the hanging file: ____________________.
decisionPointRoutines.adultWrapLine: Path one gives the character this possible choice: ____________________.

decisionPointRoutines.title: Path Two Fold
decisionPointRoutines.materials: Hanging file, path one slip, blank path two slip, and pencil.
steps: The adult points from path one to the path two blank: ____________________.
The writer invents a different path the fictional character could take: ____________________.
The adult asks how path two is different from path one: ____________________.
The writer writes path two and tucks it beside path one: ____________________.
decisionPointRoutines.adultWrapLine: Path two gives the character this other possible choice: ____________________.

decisionPointRoutines.title: Compare Clue Sort
decisionPointRoutines.materials: Hanging file, path one slip, path two slip, clue-to-compare note, and pencil.
steps: The adult lays path one and path two side by side on the table: ____________________.
The writer chooses one clue to compare before a path is picked: ____________________.
The adult asks what the clue shows about each path: ____________________.
The writer writes the clue to compare on the note: ____________________.
decisionPointRoutines.adultWrapLine: The clue to compare says this about the two paths: ____________________.

decisionPointRoutines.title: Chosen Path Slip
decisionPointRoutines.materials: Hanging file, two path slips, clue note, chosen path slip, and pencil.
steps: The adult rereads path one, path two, and the clue to compare: ____________________.
The writer picks one chosen path for the fictional character: ____________________.
The adult asks why that path fits the character choice: ____________________.
The writer writes the chosen path on the slip: ____________________.
decisionPointRoutines.adultWrapLine: The chosen path for this decision point is: ____________________.

decisionPointRoutines.title: Consequence Label Close
decisionPointRoutines.materials: Hanging file, chosen path slip, consequence note, label strip, and pencil.
steps: The adult places the chosen path slip at the front of the hanging file: ____________________.
The writer names one fictional consequence note for that chosen path: ____________________.
The adult asks what hanging-file label will help find this decision point later: ____________________.
The writer writes the consequence note and hanging-file label: ____________________.
decisionPointRoutines.adultWrapLine: The hanging-file label closes this decision point as: ____________________.

takeHomeDecisionSlips: Adult: open the hanging file and ask for one fictional character choice: ____________________.
Writer: the fictional character choice is: ____________________.

Writer: the consequence note and hanging-file label are: ____________________.

cards.kidDirection: Writer: plan one invented ferry character choice on paper and keep every river detail pretend and gentle: ____________________.
cards.choicePrompt: Character choice: name the fictional ferry guide's choice at the revision river decision point: ____________________.
cards.pathOnePrompt: Path one: write the first possible path using a revision note, ferry tag, or file marker: ____________________.
cards.pathTwoPrompt: Path two: write a different possible path using another paper crossing note or tab: ____________________.
cards.compareCluePrompt: Compare clue: name one revision clue that helps compare the two paths before choosing: ____________________.
cards.chosenPathPrompt: Chosen path: choose the path the ferry guide follows and name the clue that tipped the choice: ____________________.
cards.consequenceNotePrompt: Consequence note: write what changes on the pretend river page after the chosen path: ____________________.
cards.fileLabelPrompt: Hanging-file label: write the broad pretend label for this revision river decision point: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: fill only the choice, two path names, and hanging-file label first: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: keep the page in the hanging file and add one new consequence note later: ____________________.
